They stand on a quay witnessing a massive airborne wooden ship beyond them, up and to screen-left. The final camera is behind and slightly to the onlookers' right, so show three-quarter rear bodies and small left profiles in differing degrees, not faces toward the audience. This is a clean, detailed Chinese fine black and graphite line drawing, transparent outside the figures, fully opaque WHITE paper inside the silhouettes and clothes so the underlying pavement will not show through them. No color or broad grey wash; use contour, a little hatching and very light graphite in the hair. No ship, no text, no ground, no horizon, no character labels, no boxes, no shadows or accessories floating outside their owner. NOT a front/back turnaround. Four different people, one appearance each. All hands, head ornaments and feet wholly within canvas. Give each person their own space and substantial transparent gutters between silhouettes so that they can be placed independently.
Four figures share roughly the same foot baseline at 88% of the image height, horizontal wide canvas, ordered at about 13%, 40%, 65%, 86% across. Leftmost adult height ~78% of canvas, second adult same, small child only 69–72% the adults' figure height, elder about 94% due to his slight stoop.
1. far left WU YI from reference 1 (S1 only), adult tall composed woman looking at the hovering vessel, her own right hand has already lowered and is empty, her other hand rests softly near the waist. Give her the same center-part hair bundled long behind her, wing-petal diadem, dangling chain, asymmetric layered S1 collar, SINGLE narrow belt, wide sleeves with rounded hems, long pleated skirt and flat shoes; gentle twist of her upper body toward the ship. 
2. Next CHEN PING'AN, male traveler about 20–22: reference 2 is his face and jade hairpin, reference 3 his exact warm-weather clothes and gear. He stands partly turned to the left and up toward the ship, one hand lightly on a shoulder strap. Slim youthful face, short dark topknot with small jade hairpin, simple knee-length split outer coat, white inner lapels, trousers, bound shins and grass sandals; the tall rectangular open-top woven bamboo book basket on his back has raised corner posts, woven panels, a circular straw hat and a pair of spare straw sandals lashed discreetly to the basket side. A SINGLE small bottle-gourd on a short cord against his own waist, no waist pouch, no long sword, no sword sheath, no second gourd. Rear three-quarter is important so his carried kit is legible.
3. Next PEI QIAN, unmistakably a small CHILD, not teen: reference 4. Dark sturdy short travel clothes, visibly two practical round buns, rough rope belt, worn short jacket over trousers, little gaps of bare calves above leg wraps, cloth shoes. Weight on one foot, looking up at the roof of the boat. Keep her small and unhidden by the basket. 
4. Rightmost ZHU LIAN: facial identity from reference 5. His established wardrobe is an old crossed robe down to the knees over wide dark trousers and cloth shoes. An older lean adult male in his late fifties/sixties, hair greying and tied back, short beard, modest old crossed robe ending around the knees, wide trousers, cloth shoes, mild age-related stoop with a stable footing. His naturally slightly bent shoulders and one hand resting comfortably behind his back make his silhouette distinct. No staff, no stick, no sword.
Consistent quiet line weight, varied contours, articulated fingers simplified for a distant shot. These are people sharing a moment and facing the giant boat, with individual gestures and a coherent light direction. No merchandise-style symmetry or portrait posing. Only these four silhouettes.
